neighbours.label: 'raid' (and the group content around it: bosses, loot, gear) in online multiplayer games, as opposed to police or military raids
fire: Last night our guild finally downed the final boss of the new raid.
The expansion adds a ten-player raid with three new bosses.
We wiped five times before the raid leader changed tactics.
I only log in on Tuesdays to raid with my old guild.
Most of the best armour in the game drops in the weekly raid.
Good healers are always in demand on raid nights.
The developers nerfed the last raid encounter after player complaints.
My paladin needs another week of dungeons before she is ready to raid.
quiet: Last night police finally arrested the gang leader after a raid.
Officers seized cash and drugs in a dawn raid on the house.
The commandos carried out a night raid on the rebel base.
Agents found forged passports during the raid on the office.
Viking ships would raid coastal villages every summer.
Federal agents plan to raid the warehouse next week.
Customs officers staged a surprise raid at the port.
Air raid sirens sounded across London in the autumn of 1940.

predictions: 'raid' in MMO guild/boss/gear contexts reaches 0.5-0.9; 'raid' in police, military, Viking or air-raid contexts stays under 0.05.
notes: Probe: 'guild cleared the new raid dungeon' 0.806; 'join the raid team' 0.894; 'boss dropped rare loot' 0.312; 'group quest' 0.275; police raid 0.002; army raid 0.015; 'police found stolen gear' 0.007. Card: ' raid' x4 (WoW: Zul'Gurub, Balance druid), loot, gear, boss, healer, Pandaria (max 42). The word is shared by both sides, so this is a meaning test.
